full_judgment:
20. On examination of rival contentions and the reformulated questions of law as well as the materials on record, it appears to us the moot questions are (i) whether there is any material or evidence on record, upon which the DCT/CT (Appeal)/Tribunal could come to an estimation (a) Sale proceed of other commodity items and (b) Sale proceed of disposed of old/obsolete assets; and (ii) whether they are entitled under section 35(4) and section 83(2) of the Ordinance to make any estimation on the basis of presumption. 

 23. Now the next pertinent question comes into play, if the Assessing Officer has found as a matter of fact that complete and reliable accounts having not been placed or produced before him, having regard to that account he may proceed to estimate the assessable income of assessee. The question is how far he enjoys such authority, whether he is permitted to proceed arbitrarily on presumption and or to act based on his whim? 

 31. For ourselves, we have examined the Books of Account, but it does help the assessee to restore it’s book version, because under the relevant entry no details of specification having been mentioned in the Books of Account. Moreover, Deputy Commissioner of Taxes rejected the book version of the entry of accounts for want of reliable evidence and thereafter he proceeded to estimate the profit (income) on sale of other commodity items at his own, on the basis of presumption or pure guess and thereby he stepped outside his jurisdiction. Both the appellate authorities below without any detail discussion or specific observation upheld the said illegal estimation. Thus, it appears to us, DCT was initially justified in rejecting the Books of Account but thereafter started to step into wrong premises in estimating profit (income) on sale of other commodity items on the basis of pure guess which cannot be sustainable.
